dossier.architecture: Under-bumper acquisition, bidirectional indexer and pivoted shooter with amp/trap backpack.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve and low arm mass; numerical trajectory optimization includes module-force feedforward.
subsystems.intake: Full-width collector, wedges and passive centering rollers.
subsystems.transfer: Double-sided timing belt reverses roller directions compactly; indexer routes between two note paths.
subsystems.scoring: Independently controlled left/right shooter groups stabilize the note; rack-driven backpack scores amp and trap.
subsystems.endgame: Single-stage two-hook elevator; guiding fangs route the chain clear of the shooter/backpack.
subsystems.controls: Four AprilTag cameras on two Orange Pis; adaptive autonomous searches remaining midline notes.

versions: Prototype subsystems placed on a development robot before final packaging. Team reports roughly fifteen amp-path prototypes.
dossier.analysis: A strong integrated handoff/climb reference: chain routing must work through the entire approach sequence. Adaptive auto distinguishes a planned path from a plan that survives contested notes.
limits: Configuration description is tied to the cited interview; not a claim that every unreported shop revision is known.

context_documents.title: 2024-6328 · Routing the note and routing the chain are both architecture interfaces
context_documents.body:
# 2024-6328: Routing the note and routing the chain are both architecture interfaces

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A full-width collector uses leading rollers, wedges and slippery passive centering surfaces. The indexer selects the main shooter or rack-driven amp/trap backpack. Double-sided belts package opposite roller directions. Climb-side fangs guide the chain over areas where it could catch the shooter/backpack; four pose cameras use deliberately different views/lenses.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The source explicitly connects the fangs to avoiding chain entrapment and the camera arrangement to useful tag visibility on approach to scoring locations. It treats camera placement as a deliberate strategy choice rather than simply adding identical cameras.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A compact scorer and climber can each work separately but fail when a flexible chain sweeps through their shared space. Passive routing surfaces are therefore a mechanism interface, not cosmetic guards. Similarly, extra cameras help only when their sight lines and uncertainty provide information the existing views lack.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test chain capture with lateral error and robot roll, inspect every backpack handoff, and measure pose availability along the intended routes rather than only at a parked test position.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/4BlE5zDQwBE](https://youtu.be/4BlE5zDQwBE)

source_reviews.title: Mechanical Advantage February CAD update
facts: Opposing roller directions route the note between speaker and amp backpack. The fourth intake revision used removable dead-axle rollers.
Pivot work added motor and bolt-head clearance and used standard spacers. The arm grew for climb reach.
The team prioritized low center of mass and presented provisional CAD estimates.
source_reviews.limitations: Build-stage values and intended climber reduction are not final hardware certification.

source_reviews.title: Mechanical Advantage post-Championship Q&A
facts: Four OV2311 cameras, including a zoom view intended to help long-range speaker-side localization. LEDs and rumble report secure note possession.
source_reviews.limitations: Camera model and use do not establish measured accuracy or all event wiring.

source_reviews.title: Presto public code update
source_reviews.facts: Team describes RobotCode2024Public as the latest published 2024 code.
source_reviews.limitations: Repository release date is distinct from deployment date.

source_reviews.title: Mechanical Advantage Behind the Bumpers
facts: The dossier describes an under-bumper collector, two-direction indexer, pivoted differential launcher, rack backpack and two-hook climber.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Presto used one intake to feed a moving scoring arm. The February team post explains how a roller set can send the note into the speaker shooter or amp backpack by changing roller directions. The approach leaves room for a separate placement receiver while keeping the note-path decision inside the robot. The arm also carries substantial hardware for endgame. The team lengthened it for chain reach and tracked modeled center of mass because the robot still needed to drive hard during the primary scoring cycle.
piece_flow: Inherited under-bumper roller, wedges and passive contacts catch and center the note.
The February roller indexer sends it toward the launcher or amp backpack. Direction is the routing choice.
The inherited rack mechanism extends for amp or trap. The chain guides keep engagement away from the backpack and shooter during the climb.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Mounting several mechanisms on the arm makes its travel a shared constraint. A longer arm helps hook reach but increases sweep and can increase holding torque. The team used provisional arm-up and arm-down CAD comparisons before adding the backpack. For transfer, measure loaded swing and stowed height after the mechanism, wiring, bumpers and battery are in place.

subsystems.name: Dead-axle pickup
subsystems.construction: Fourth-revision CAD update describes rollers removed by two outside bolts without taking tube plugs out.
subsystems.operation: Capture the note and swap a damaged roller as an assembly.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team emphasized service and keeping the remaining parts together during removal.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The short service sequence matters only if bolts can be reached with bumpers and mounts installed. Roller replacement must restore its feed height without adjustment.
subsystems.interfaces: Outer bolt tool access, tube/plug retention and roller-to-indexer gap.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Time a swap and test loaded feed immediately after. Check whether damaged mounts can trap the roller.
subsystems.unknowns: Final roller construction, impact data and service time.

subsystems.name: Bidirectional indexer and arm
subsystems.construction: Build update describes opposed roller directions on an arm with low-mounted pivot. Inherited study supplies the backpack rack and differential shooter.
subsystems.operation: Stage and route to either scoring mechanism, then move the arm to its release pose.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team highlighted path selection by changing roller motion, and increased arm reach for climbing.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A simple routing command still depends on enough contact overlap through the reversal. Check orientation changes and whether an occupied branch can be recognized and cleared.
subsystems.interfaces: Stationary intake-to-moving-arm interface, shooter entrance and backpack receiver.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test stalled and partially transferred notes in both branches. Inspect pivot bolt-head access and encoder alignment after repairs.
subsystems.unknowns: Final retention and sensor thresholds, exact pivot sweep and loaded geometry.

subsystems.name: Localization and chain interface
subsystems.construction: Team describes four cameras with one zoom view. Inherited chain fangs and paired hooks guide engagement.
subsystems.operation: Maintain pose estimates and bring the arm-mounted chain tool into alignment.
subsystems.team_rationale: Zoom supports seeing speaker tags farther away. Earlier arm work addressed reach.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A narrow view adds distance only within a limited pointing envelope. Chain guides improve placement only if the load engages the intended geometry instead of pushing into the backpack.
subsystems.interfaces: Chassis heading, tag visibility, chain trajectory and backpack clearance.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test frame contact and one-hook engagement separately from static CAD. Confirm localization behavior when the zoom view is occluded.
subsystems.unknowns: Final climb load path and accuracy with lost tags.

revisions: February changes included service access around the pivot, longer arms and the fourth intake revision. A later release names Presto and points to the latest public code.
transferable_principles: Choose routing by reversible contact when the same staged note can be controlled in both branches. Preserve independent service access for rollers and pivot hardware.
disconfirming_conditions: A larger or stiffer game piece can bridge the branch. Extra arm reach may cost too much inertia and travel clearance for the primary scoring route.
remaining_gaps: Final code behavior, installed chain path, full captions and event-specific hardware states.
recommended_images: Build post 208 indexer and intake assembly images
Loaded chain path around the backpack
